answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond in escrow before it can earn. Like an ember banked under ash, the bond sits idle but real: it returns only after honest work. One operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must split capital across all of them, while each jade-green newcomer earns at the lowest rate until its bond seasons. Misbehavior triggers a slash, and the ferrous ledger records every forfeiture, so reputation follows the wallet, not the name. One fake identity is cheap; an army is ruinously expensive.
